newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian money market quiet on bank staff strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian money market quiet on bank staff strike.

text.p: The Indian call money market was largely inactive on Friday as most banks were shut on account of a nationwide strike by their staff, dealers said.
They said a few foreign and private banks were open but could not transact any business, they said.
"There were no quotes today," one dealer said.
There was little demand for funds as Friday was the fortnightly reporting day for banks, but some lending institutions were keen on lending three day money, another dealer said.
Bank trade unions had called for a one-day strike to protest against the government's plan to permit private banks to set up branches in rural areas.
There were some trades in governemnt securities for next-day value, dealers said.
The 13.80 percent government stock 2002 rose to 106.30 rupees from 106.25 rupees and the 12.14 percent 2000 to 102.05 from 102.00, dealers said.
Treasury bills maturing in July 1998 yielded 8.68 to 8.70 percent against the auctioned yield of 8.85 percent, dealers said.
Commercial paper for top-rated companies was quoted at 8.00/8.25 percent for 30 days, 8.35/8.60 percent for 45 days, 8.95/9.15 percent for 60 days and 9.25/9.5 percent for three months, dealers said.
